# Project Overview

Creatinine-to-cystatin C discordance and adverse events in patients receiving
platinum-based chemotherapy.

The project repeats the Jiaxuan analysis at **two cohort levels off one
pipeline**: the **entire cohort** (N = 943, all tumour stages) and the
**Local/Early** cohort (N = 323, advanced/metastatic patients excluded). Every
exposure, model, table, figure and download is carried over unchanged at both
levels; both use the newer 2022P001091 creatinine pull and carry the CKD / ESKD
/ AKI variable family ported from the ICI-CKD project.

| | Details |
|---|---|
| **Entire cohort** | no stage filter — N = 943 |
| **Local/Early cohort** | `tumor_stage == "Local/Early"` (stage I–II / local / neoadjuvant) — N = 323 |
| **Excluded from the Local/Early pages** | `tumor_stage == "Advanced/Metastatic"` (stage III–IV) — 620 patients |
| **Primary exposure** | `egfr_diff_pct_per10` — eGFR difference (%) per 10-percentage-point decline |
| **Follow-up** | 90 days from baseline sample date |
| **Framework** | Competing risks (death as competing event for non-fatal outcomes) |
| **Parent project** | [Jiaxuan project](https://tianqi-ouyang.github.io/Cys-C-project-/) |

# Pages and Cohort Sizes

The project runs at two cohort levels off the same pipeline. Both use the
2022P001091 creatinine pull and carry the full CKD / ESKD / AKI variable family.

| Page | Cohort | N |
|---|---|---|
| [**Entire Cohort**](qmd/ritu_entire.qmd) | all platinum, **all stages** | **943** |
| [Whole Cohort](qmd/ritu_whole.qmd) | all platinum, Local/Early only | **323** |
| [Carboplatin Cohort](qmd/ritu_carbo.qmd) | carboplatin, Local/Early | **190** |
| [Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3](qmd/ritu_carbo_auc3.qmd) | carboplatin AUC ≥ 3, Local/Early | **143** |

Entire cohort: 323 Local/Early + 620 Advanced/Metastatic; 596 carboplatin,
347 cisplatin. Within the 323 Local/Early: 190 carboplatin, 133 cisplatin.

**`tumor_stage` differs between the two levels.** It is constant in the
Local/Early cohort, so it is dropped from Table 1 and from every adjuster set
there. In the entire cohort it varies, so it is restored — which makes the
entire-cohort page's model specification the same as the Jiaxuan project's, but
run on the newer creatinine pull and with the kidney variables added. Comparing
the two pages shows what the stage restriction does.

# Exclusion Flow

Inherited from the Jiaxuan pipeline:

1. REDCap records restricted to EMPIs present in `N=596 for tianqi.xlsx` → 946
2. Patients with no matching RPDR lab records excluded (2) → 944
3. Missing baseline cystatin C (`cys_c_baseline` = NA) excluded
4. Missing platinum group (`platin_group` = NA) excluded
5. Record 911 dropped (all RPDR pre-baseline labs fall outside the 45-day window) → **943 = entire cohort**
6. `tumor_stage != "Local/Early"` excluded (620) → **323 = Local/Early cohort**

`ritu_data.qmd` saves after both step 5 (`ritu_full_master.rds`) and step 6
(`ritu_final_master.rds`), so the two cohort levels come from one pipeline run
and are identical in every variable definition.

Details in [Data Management](qmd/ritu_data.qmd).

# What Changed Relative to the Jiaxuan Project

Four kinds of change, nothing else:

**1. Cohort source.** `ritu_data.qmd` applies the stage restriction and writes
`ritu_final_master.rds`; the three analysis pages read that file.

**2. `tumor_stage` dropped as a covariate.** It is constant within this cohort,
so it carries no information and would make the design matrix rank-deficient.
It is removed from Table 1 and from the adjuster set of every Fine-Gray,
cause-specific hazard, Cox PH and linear-subHR model.

**3. Two covariate fixes on the AUC ≥ 3 page only.** That subgroup's filter
empties the `cancer_type_cat_7` "GI" level (0 of 143) and leaves `steroids`
constant at 1 (all 143 received steroids). Together these made the design matrix
rank-deficient — rank 19 of 21 — so `cmprsk::crr` failed for *every* outcome,
including composite grade 2 AEs with 64 events, while the formula interface
silently returned blank coefficient rows. `droplevels()` is re-applied after the
cohort filter and `steroids` is dropped from that page's adjuster sets (it stays
as a descriptive Table 1 row). The whole and carboplatin cohorts are full rank
throughout and keep the original adjuster set.

**4. Sparse-outcome guards.** Several outcomes have very few events in 323
patients (90-day death = 2). Each model helper is wrapped so that a model which
cannot be estimated emits a short note instead of aborting the render. No model
specification is altered.

Unchanged: primary and sensitivity exposures, the `dose_discrep_per25increase`
predictor in the carboplatin pages, reference categories (`sex` = Female,
`ecog_score_cat2` = "0"), the competing-risks framework, Cox PH for 90-day
death, eGFR capping rules, 2.5/97.5-percentile plot trimming, Word and
PowerPoint downloads, and all section numbering.

# Power Caveats — Local/Early pages only

These follow arithmetically from the **323-patient** cohort and apply to the
Local/Early pages. The [entire-cohort page](qmd/ritu_entire.qmd) has roughly 3×
the events and is not affected in the same way — most notably 90-day death has
**41 events there versus 2** here, so its models are worth reading on that page
and not on this one.

The analyses are reported as specified; read the sparse ones with the event
counts in view.

| Outcome | Events in 323 | Multivariable estimate |
|---|---|---|
| Composite grade 2 AEs | 149 | adequately powered |
| Anemia grade 2 | 138 | adequately powered |
| Overall hospitalization | 68 | borderline |
| Platinum-related hospitalization | 46 | over-parameterised |
| Composite grade 3 AEs | 43 | over-parameterised |
| Anemia grade 3 | 40 | over-parameterised |
| Thrombocytopenia grade 2 | 37 | over-parameterised |
| AKI (KDIGO) | 33 | over-parameterised |
| AKI grade 2 | 26 | over-parameterised |
| Thrombocytopenia grade 3 | 9 | not interpretable |
| Individual hospitalization reasons | 5–25 | not interpretable |
| **90-day death** | **2** | **not estimable** |

The multivariable models carry roughly 20 covariate degrees of freedom against a
conventional target of 10 events per covariate. Univariable columns remain
readable throughout.

Two further consequences worth stating in any write-up:

- **90-day mortality is 2/323 (0.6 %).** Early-stage patients rarely die within
  90 days of starting platinum — a finding in its own right, not just a
  limitation.
- **The competing-risks correction barely bites.** With death nearly absent,
  Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards and cause-specific hazards are close to
  identical in this cohort.

# Outcomes

## Grade 2/3 Adverse Events (within 90 days)

| Outcome | Definition |
|---|---|
| Anemia grade 2 | HGB < 10 g/dL |
| Anemia grade 3 | HGB < 8 g/dL |
| Thrombocytopenia grade 2 | PLT < 75 x10^9/L |
| Thrombocytopenia grade 3 | PLT < 50 x10^9/L |
| AKI grade 2 | Post-baseline CRE > 1.5x pre-baseline CRE (KDIGO) |
| AKI grade 3 | Post-baseline CRE > 3.0x pre-baseline CRE (KDIGO) |
| Composite grade 2 | Any of anemia/thrombocytopenia/AKI grade 2 |
| Composite grade 3 | Any of anemia/thrombocytopenia/AKI grade 3 |

## Hospitalizations & Mortality

- **Hospitalizations:** 11 reason categories; reasons 1–7 define `side_effect` (platinum-related)
- **90-day mortality** (`death_90`): derived from `pt_status` and `days_last_follow_up`
- All outcomes above censored at 90 days

## Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)

Ported from the [ICI-CKD project](https://tianqi-ouyang.github.io/ICI-CKD-/data_management.html),
re-anchored to `baseline_sample_date`. **These are the only outcomes in the
project that are not censored at 90 days** — a qualifying CKD episode must be
*sustained for ≥ 90 days*, so they use the full length of RPDR creatinine
follow-up (median 446 days, max 1167).

| Outcome | Definition | n (%) of 323 |
|---|---|---|
| `aki` | CRE > 1.5 × median of prior 90 d, **or** ≥ 0.3 mg/dL above the prior-2-day low | 63 (19.5 %) |
| `ckd_incidence` | Sustained ≥ 90 d: `pct_drop > 0.30` & eGFR < 60 & baseline eGFR ≥ 60 | 15 (4.6 %) |
| `ckd_progression` | Sustained ≥ 90 d: eGFR < 60 & baseline eGFR < 60 | 20 (6.2 %) |
| `eskd_defination_1` | Sustained ≥ 90 d: eGFR < 10 | 1 (0.3 %) |
| `esrd_kt_after_ici` | ESRD / KT / dialysis ICD code after baseline | 1 (0.3 %) |
| `eskd_composite` | `esrd_kt_after_ici == 1 \| eskd_defination_1 == 1` | 1 (0.3 %) |
| `ckd_composite` | `eskd_composite == 1 \| ckd_incidence == 1 \| ckd_progression == 1` | 35 (10.8 %) |

All of the above are **Table 1 rows** on all three analysis pages, together with
`esrd_kt` (ESRD / KT at or before baseline, n = 1), `eGFR_CRE_baseline`,
`ckd_stage_baseline` and `last_cre_days`. They also keep a dedicated section —
2.2 on the whole-cohort page, 3.2 on the carboplatin pages — carrying the median
time to each event, the length of creatinine follow-up, and the `aki` vs
`AKI_kdigo_90days` cross-tabulation that Table 1 cannot show.

They are descriptive only: **not** in any Fine-Gray, cause-specific or Cox model,
because mixing a full-follow-up outcome into the 90-day competing-risks framework
would need its own censoring and competing-event decisions.

`aki` is a different variable from the existing `AKI_g2_90days` /
`AKI_kdigo_90days`: it compares each creatinine against the patient's own
preceding 90-day median across the whole record, not against a fixed
pre-baseline value inside 90 days. In the whole cohort they agree on 19
patients, `aki` alone flags 44, and `AKI_kdigo_90days` alone flags 14.

# Data Sources

| Source | Used for |
|---|---|
| REDCap export `CystatinCInPatientsO_DATA_2026-04-27_0819.csv` | Baseline, treatment, outcomes |
| RPDR **2022P001091** (`mes98_0728261259…`, Aug 2026) | **All creatinine** — 48,843 rows |
| RPDR **2026-03-19** (`mes98_0318261449…`) | HGB, PLT, ALB, GHBA1C (128,156 rows), plus all diagnoses and medications |

The newer pull is a creatinine-only extract — it has no `Dia` or `Med` file and
no HGB/PLT/ALB/GHBA1C — so it supplies creatinine and the original pull supplies
everything else. Both cover the same 973 EMPIs over 1989–2026; the newer one has
~2,800 more creatinine values, which is what the longitudinal eGFR, CKD and AKI
outcomes are built from.

# Key Variables

## Exposure

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `egfr_diff_pct` | 100 × (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed − Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault |
| `egfr_diff_pct_per10` | Primary reporting scale: per 10-percentage-point **decline** |
| `egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10` | Sensitivity: CKD-EPI 2012 CysC vs CKD-EPI 2021 Cr, per 10 % decline |
| `dose_discrep_per25increase` | Carboplatin dose discrepancy (actual − predicted mg) / 25 |

## eGFR & Kidney Function

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `baseline_cre_egfr` | CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²) |
| `ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys` | CKD-EPI 2012 combined creatinine + cystatin C eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²) |
| `ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex` | Combined CKD-EPI eGFR adjusted for BSA (mL/min) |
| `cockcroft` | Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance |
| `ckd_stage_cre` | KDIGO G-stage from `baseline_cre_egfr` (G3a / G3b kept apart) |
| `ckd_stage_cre_cys` | KDIGO G-stage from `ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys` (G3a / G3b kept apart) |
| `eGFR_CRE_baseline` | CKD-EPI creatinine eGFR at `pre_CRE_45days` — the baseline the CKD outcomes are referenced to |
| `ckd_stage_baseline` | KDIGO stage from `eGFR_CRE_baseline`, ICI-CKD convention (G3a + G3b collapsed into one stage 3) |

Only `ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex` is capped at 125 mL/min; the indexed value
and `cockcroft` are uncapped. Uncapped values feed the eGFR difference; capped
values feed the dose-discrepancy calculation.

Both CKD stage variables use the standard KDIGO G categories — G1 ≥ 90,
G2 60–89, G3a 45–59, G3b 30–44, G4 15–29, G5 < 15 mL/min/1.73m² — and are built
from the **BSA-indexed** eGFRs, the scale KDIGO staging is defined on. No patient
in this cohort reaches G5, so that level is dropped rather than shown as an empty
Table 1 row. They are descriptive Table 1 rows only; no model adjusts for them
(the continuous eGFRs already appear in the adjuster sets).

## Competing Risk Variables

| Pattern | Description |
|---|---|
| `cmp_time_<outcome>` | Time for the competing-risk model |
| `cmp_status_<outcome>` | 0 = censored, 1 = event, 2 = death |
